questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed in the syllabus coverage for “Password Management”?
options: Why passwords must not be stored as plaintext
Password reset and account recovery design
questions.answer_key: Why passwords must not be stored as plaintext
questions.explanation: The attached FastAPI syllabus lists “Why passwords must not be stored as plaintext” under this lesson. The remaining syllabus subtopics are preserved in the lesson file for complete coverage.

questions.prompt: According to the worked example in “Password Management”, which result should the learner verify?
options: Without Authorization: Bearer <token>, the request is rejected. This demo does not authenticate or authorize the token.
The app publishes itself to production and passes all tests automatically.
HTTP 500 is returned for every valid request.
Input validation and authorization are disabled by design.
questions.answer_key: Without Authorization: Bearer <token>, the request is rejected. This demo does not authenticate or authorize the token.
questions.explanation: The worked example explicitly documents this expected result. Reproduce it locally in the listed environment before treating it as tested behavior.

questions.prompt: Which security action should a production implementation take? (Password Management)
options: Verify identity credentials and enforce resource-level authorization on the server
Trust any decoded token because it contains JSON
Store passwords in plaintext to allow recovery
Hide buttons in the frontend and skip backend permission checks
questions.answer_key: Verify identity credentials and enforce resource-level authorization on the server
questions.explanation: Security schemes wire the request flow but do not replace cryptographic token validation, password hashing or access-control checks.
